objective: Learners draft a one-page skills profile listing real skills, activities, and responsibilities from their own life, organized under the same four headings a résumé uses (skills, activities, responsibilities, and interests), as a foundation for a future first résumé.
scenario: The learner lists their own genuine skills and experiences, such as babysitting a younger sibling, a sport, a school project, or a volunteer task, and organizes them under four headings the way a résumé would, without inventing any experience they have not actually had.
safetyNotes: No last name, address, phone number, or other identifying contact information is required on this practice document.
materials: the four-heading template on this task sheet

tasks.directions: Before organizing, brainstorm freely for two minutes.

prompts.text: List as many real things you have done, learned, or been responsible for as you can think of in two minutes, without sorting them yet.

tasks.directions: Sort your brainstormed list under four headings: Skills, Activities, Responsibilities, Interests. Write at least two real items under each heading.

prompts.text: I wrote at least two real items under each of the four headings.
Every item is something I have actually done or am actually responsible for, not something invented to sound impressive.

tasks.directions: Pick your strongest item overall and describe it in one specific sentence a stranger could understand.

prompts.text: Write one specific sentence describing your strongest item, naming what you did and one concrete result or detail.

tasks.directions: Think about what you noticed while brainstorming.

prompts.text: Was it easier or harder than you expected to list your own skills and experiences? Explain why, and name one item you had forgotten about until this task.

remediation: If a learner's items stay vague ('I'm responsible,' 'I'm good at sports'), reteach by asking three follow-up questions for one item together (what specifically, how often, what was the result) and having the learner rewrite that one item with the added specifics before revising the rest.
extension: Have the learner rewrite their two strongest items as full résumé-style bullet points starting with an action verb, following an example the adult or lesson provides.
